concepts.title: Indefinite Integral as Anti-derivative
concepts.definition: The mathematical operation that determines the set of all antiderivatives for a given function, differing only by an additive constant.
concepts.formula: integral(f(x) dx) = F(x) + C where F'(x) = f(x)
concepts.key_idea: Integration acts as the mathematical reverse of differentiation.
question_patterns: find the anti derivative of the function
write an anti derivative using the method of inspection
integrate the given function with respect to x
find the indefinite integral of the expression
Explain the method of Indefinite Integral as Anti-derivative.

solution_steps.action: Identify the given integrand function f(x)
solution_steps.explain: Determine the function that needs to be integrated.

solution_steps.action: Find a function F(x) whose derivative equals f(x)
solution_steps.explain: Use standard differentiation formulas in reverse or inspection to find the primitive function.

solution_steps.action: Add the constant of integration C
solution_steps.explain: Since the derivative of any constant is zero, the general antiderivative is F(x) + C.

concepts.title: Integration by Substitution
concepts.definition: A technique that simplifies an integral by replacing a variable and its differential with a new variable, typically chosen because its derivative is present in the integrand.
concepts.key_idea: Transform the variable of integration to match a standard formula.
question_patterns: integrate the function by substitution
find the integral by changing the variable of integration
evaluate the integral using a suitable substitution
use substitution to simplify and integrate
Explain the method of Integration by Substitution.

solution_steps.action: Choose a suitable substitution u = g(x)
solution_steps.explain: Look for a part of the integrand whose derivative also appears in the integrand.

solution_steps.action: Compute the differential du = g'(x) dx
solution_steps.explain: Differentiate the substitution equation to relate dx to du.

solution_steps.action: Rewrite the entire integral in terms of u and du
solution_steps.explain: Substitute u and du into the original integral to obtain a simpler form.

solution_steps.action: Integrate with respect to u and then substitute back
solution_steps.explain: Find the antiderivative in terms of u, and then replace u with g(x) to get the final answer.

concepts.title: Integration using Trigonometric Identities
concepts.definition: The method of rewriting products or powers of sine, cosine, and other trigonometric functions into simpler linear terms using standard trig formulas.
concepts.key_idea: Convert higher powers of trigonometric functions into linear terms.
question_patterns: integrate the trigonometric function
evaluate the integral using trigonometric identities
find the integral of powers of sine and cosine
simplify the trigonometric integrand and integrate
Explain the method of Integration using Trigonometric Identities.

solution_steps.action: Identify the powers or products of trigonometric terms in the integrand
solution_steps.explain: Determine which trigonometric functions are present and their powers.

solution_steps.action: Apply standard trigonometric identities to reduce the powers
solution_steps.explain: Use double-angle, half-angle, or product-to-sum formulas to rewrite the integrand as a sum of linear trigonometric terms.

solution_steps.action: Integrate each term individually using standard formulas
solution_steps.explain: Find the antiderivative of each simplified term and add the integration constant.

concepts.title: Standard Integrals of Particular Rational Functions
concepts.definition: A collection of pre-derived integration formulas for specific algebraic fractions, particularly those containing quadratic expressions in the denominator.
concepts.key_idea: Match the quadratic denominator to one of the standard algebraic forms.
question_patterns: integrate the rational function of quadratic form
find the integral of 1 over a quadratic expression
evaluate the integral using standard quadratic formulas
calculate the integral of the form dx over x^2 minus a^2
Explain the method of Standard Integrals of Particular Rational Functions.

solution_steps.action: Express the denominator in the standard form x^2 +/- a^2 or a^2 - x^2
solution_steps.explain: If the denominator is a general quadratic, complete the square to write it in terms of a squared linear variable and a constant.

solution_steps.action: Identify the matching standard formula
solution_steps.explain: Compare the transformed integral with the list of standard integrals for quadratic denominators.

solution_steps.action: Apply the formula and write the final expression
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the variable and constant into the standard formula and add the constant of integration.

concepts.title: Integration by Partial Fractions
concepts.definition: An algebraic method used to break down a complex rational function into a sum of simpler fractions that can be integrated directly using standard rules.
concepts.key_idea: Decompose rational expressions into simpler, integrable components.
question_patterns: integrate using partial fractions
resolve the rational function into partial fractions and integrate
find the integral of the rational expression
evaluate the integral of a proper rational function
Explain the method of Integration by Partial Fractions.

solution_steps.action: Check if the rational function is proper
solution_steps.explain: Ensure the degree of the numerator is less than the degree of the denominator. If not, perform polynomial long division first.

solution_steps.action: Factor the denominator completely
solution_steps.explain: Express the denominator as a product of linear and/or irreducible quadratic factors.

solution_steps.action: Set up the partial fraction decomposition
solution_steps.explain: Assign unknown constants (A, B, C, etc.) to each factor according to standard decomposition rules.

solution_steps.action: Solve for the unknown constants
solution_steps.explain: Multiply by the common denominator and equate coefficients or substitute specific values of x to find the constants.

solution_steps.action: Integrate the resulting simpler fractions
solution_steps.explain: Use standard logarithmic or inverse trigonometric formulas to integrate each term.

concepts.title: Integration by Parts
concepts.definition: An integration technique based on the product rule of differentiation, used to integrate the product of two functions by choosing one to differentiate and the other to integrate.
concepts.formula: integral(u * v dx) = u * integral(v dx) - integral(u' * integral(v dx) dx)
concepts.key_idea: Differentiate the simpler function and integrate the other.
question_patterns: integrate the product of two functions
evaluate the integral using integration by parts
find the integral of x times a trigonometric function
calculate the integral of a logarithmic or inverse trigonometric function
Explain the method of Integration by Parts.

solution_steps.action: Choose the first function u and the second function v
solution_steps.explain: Use the ILATE rule (Inverse trigonometric, Logarithmic, Algebraic, Trigonometric, Exponential) to select u.

solution_steps.action: Find the derivative of u and the integral of v
solution_steps.explain: Compute du/dx and find the antiderivative of v.

solution_steps.action: Apply the integration by parts formula
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the components into the formula: u * integral(v) - integral(u' * integral(v)).

solution_steps.action: Evaluate the remaining integral
solution_steps.explain: Complete the integration of the second term and add the constant of integration.

concepts.title: Special Exponential Integral
concepts.definition: A specific integration shortcut for integrands of the form e^x multiplied by the sum of a function and its derivative, yielding e^x times the function.
concepts.formula: integral(e^x * (f(x) + f'(x)) dx) = e^x * f(x) + C
concepts.key_idea: Identify the function and its derivative to write the solution directly.
question_patterns: integrate e^x times a function and its derivative
find the integral of the form e^x (f(x) + f'(x))
evaluate the exponential product integral
use the special e^x integration rule
Explain the method of Special Exponential Integral.

solution_steps.action: Identify the function f(x) and its derivative f'(x) in the integrand
solution_steps.explain: Check if the expression inside the parentheses can be written as f(x) + f'(x).

solution_steps.action: Write the result directly using the standard theorem
solution_steps.explain: The integral of e^x * (f(x) + f'(x)) is simply e^x * f(x) + C.

solution_steps.action: Add the constant of integration and verify the result
solution_steps.explain: Differentiate e^x * f(x) to confirm it returns the original integrand, confirming the antiderivative is correct.

concepts.title: Quadratic Square Root Types
concepts.definition: Standard formulas for integrating functions containing square roots of quadratic expressions, derived using integration by parts or trigonometric substitution.
concepts.key_idea: Use standard formulas for square roots of quadratic polynomials.
question_patterns: integrate the square root of a quadratic expression
find the integral of sqrt(x^2 + a^2) dx
evaluate the integral of sqrt(a^2 - x^2) dx
calculate the integral of a quadratic square root form
Explain the method of Quadratic Square Root Types.

solution_steps.action: Express the quadratic expression inside the square root in standard form
solution_steps.explain: Complete the square if necessary to write the expression as x^2 +/- a^2 or a^2 - x^2.

solution_steps.action: Apply the corresponding standard square root integration formula
solution_steps.explain: Substitute the variable and constant values into the pre-derived formula.

solution_steps.action: Add the constant of integration to the result
solution_steps.explain: Since this is an indefinite integral, append + C to the antiderivative expression.

concepts.title: Definite Integral of a Linear Function
concepts.definition: Evaluating the net area under a straight-line function over a given interval by finding its antiderivative and calculating the difference between the upper and lower limits.
concepts.key_idea: Integrate the linear and constant terms separately and evaluate at limits.
question_patterns: evaluate the definite integral of {p} x + {q} from {a} to {b}
find the value of integral of {p}*x + {q} with limits {a} and {b}
calculate the definite integral of {p}x + {q} dx between {a} and {b}
what is the definite integral of {p}x + {q} from {a} to {b}
Explain the method of Definite Integral of a Linear Function.

solution_steps.action: Compute the integral of the linear term p*x
solution_steps.explain: The antiderivative of p*x is p * x^2 / 2. Evaluating this from a to b gives p * (b^2 - a^2) / 2.

solution_steps.action: Compute the integral of the constant term q
solution_steps.explain: The antiderivative of q is q * x. Evaluating this from a to b gives q * (b - a).

solution_steps.action: Sum the two terms to find the total definite integral
solution_steps.explain: Add the evaluated linear term and constant term to get the final value.

concepts.title: Definite Integral of a Quadratic Power Function
concepts.definition: Calculating the definite integral of a quadratic term by applying the power rule of integration and evaluating the resulting cubic expression at the boundary limits.
concepts.key_idea: Apply the power rule to the quadratic term and find the difference of cubes.
question_patterns: evaluate the definite integral of {p} x^2 from {a} to {b}
find the value of integral of {p}*x^2 with limits {a} and {b}
calculate the definite integral of {p}x^2 dx between {a} and {b}
what is the definite integral of {p}x^2 from {a} to {b}
Explain the method of Definite Integral of a Quadratic Power Function.

solution_steps.action: Compute the difference of cubes of the limits
solution_steps.explain: The antiderivative of x^2 is x^3 / 3, so we first find b^3 - a^3.

solution_steps.action: Multiply by coefficient p and divide by 3
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the difference of cubes by p and divide by 3 to get the final definite integral.

solution_steps.action: Report the definite integral value
solution_steps.explain: The result is the net signed area under the curve p*x^2 between the limits a and b.

concepts.title: Properties of Definite Integrals
concepts.definition: A set of rules that simplify the evaluation of definite integrals, including interval splitting, change of variables, and symmetry properties for even and odd functions.
concepts.formula: integral(a to b, f(x) dx) = -integral(b to a, f(x) dx)
concepts.key_idea: Use interval splitting and symmetry to simplify definite integral calculations.
question_patterns: evaluate the definite integral using properties
show that the definite integral is zero using symmetry
simplify the definite integral using properties of limits
find the integral using the property of even and odd functions
Explain the method of Properties of Definite Integrals.

solution_steps.action: Identify the limits of integration and the integrand function
solution_steps.explain: Check if the limits are symmetric [-a, a] or if the integrand has periodic properties.

solution_steps.action: Apply the appropriate definite integral property
solution_steps.explain: Use properties like splitting the interval, replacing x with (a+b-x), or checking if the function is even/odd to simplify the integral.

solution_steps.action: Evaluate the simplified integral
solution_steps.explain: Compute the final value of the simplified definite integral.
